request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change that moves anyone's claimed or due-total now writes `ROLLUP` lines to the audit, and a `TOTALS` line when the sheet's totals move. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The change is server-only. Until now these figures were only worked out in the browser, so I added a new service, `rollup/Rollup.java`, that works them out on the server the same way:
- **Claimed:** the sum of a person's open and settled claims.
- **Due-total:** for each claim, its settled figure, else its stated figure, else its amount at the rate in force on its date. It shows `n/a` when the person's grade has no rate today and none of their claims has a fixed figure.

For each change it records the figures before, makes the change, recalculates, and writes only what moved:
- **Order:** the lines are written only if the change goes through, and always after the change's own line.
- **People:** one `ROLLUP` line each, in the order they were added; someone just added always gets one.
- **Totals:** a `TOTALS` line only if the sheet's claimed-total or due-total changed.

So a change that moves nothing writes no extra lines, and changing the sheet's today writes lines only when figures move.

It's hooked into every service that changes data: changing today, adding or editing a person, setting a rate, adding or editing a claim, changing a claim's status, and taking a statement.

The audit lines use `person=<name>` rather than the `name=<name>` written in the change request, because that's what the test spec expects.
